hunks.baseline: The treasured blade had been a gift from his father—the first and last he had ever received from him. Its owner had been only a boy in his teens, yet he had distinguished himself so early that his youth hardly mattered. Now the blade followed its master’s hand and cut cleanly through the target before him.
hunks.sol: It was the first and last treasured blade his father had given him. He had been only a boy in his teens then, though he’d distinguished himself so early that his youth hardly mattered. Now the blade followed its master’s hand and cut cleanly through the target before him.

hunks.baseline: Blood sprayed with a cold, slicing sound. A pair of eyes that had watched the whole thing sank deeply.
hunks.sol: Blood sprayed with a cold slicing sound. The eyes that had watched it all grew dark.

hunks.baseline: “What have you done?”
hunks.sol: “What are you doing?”

hunks.baseline: The question held a great many things, but the answer was simple.
hunks.sol: The question held a great deal, but the answer was simple.

hunks.baseline: “Because this isn’t the path I want.”
hunks.sol: “Choosing a different path.”

hunks.baseline: Sama Pyo let go of the hilt, already cold beneath his hand.
hunks.sol: Sama Pyo let go of the hilt, cold beneath his hand.

hunks.baseline: The keen blade, a weapon permitted only to the heir of the Black Dragon Demon Gate, had passed just beside Sima Gong’s nose and cut through the pool of blood.
hunks.sol: The keen blade, permitted only to the heir of the Black Dragon Demon Gate, had grazed the bridge of Sima Gong’s nose and cut through the pool of blood.

hunks.baseline: As if mocking the father who had been glad to see his son become a true man of the unorthodox faction—and had willingly accepted death.
hunks.sol: As if mocking the father who had rejoiced to see his son become a true man of the unorthodox faction—and had willingly accepted death.

hunks.baseline: “This is my choice. The path I, Sama Pyo, have chosen—the man who will succeed you as Sect Leader of the Black Dragon Demon Gate.”
hunks.sol: “This is my choice. The path I, Sama Pyo, have chosen as the man who will succeed you as Sect Leader of the Black Dragon Demon Gate.”

hunks.baseline: Sama Pyo calmly met Sima Gong’s gaze as he shouted, his voice boiling with blood.
hunks.sol: Sama Pyo calmly met Sima Gong’s gaze as his father shouted, his voice thick with blood.

hunks.baseline: “Because it isn’t what comes first, or what is best.”
hunks.sol: “Because what comes first isn’t necessarily what’s best.”

hunks.baseline: It was a question of what was right—and what was better.
hunks.sol: It was a question of what was right—of what was better.

hunks.baseline: “I’d forgotten for my whole life. No—I’d grown so used to it that I kept pretending not to know. But not anymore.”
hunks.sol: “I forgot that for most of my life. No, I’d grown so used to things as they were that I kept pretending not to know. But not anymore.”

hunks.baseline: They were family, bound by the same blood, and rivals competing for the one and only position of heir. They were little more than soldiers, obeying the one man who had given them that blood.
hunks.sol: They were family, bound by blood, and rivals competing for the one position of heir. They were little more than soldiers obeying the man who had given them that blood.

hunks.baseline: The kind of people who sometimes had to face even death without hesitation.
hunks.sol: Soldiers who sometimes had to face even death.

hunks.baseline: No one knew that the Black Dragon Demon Gate’s youngest young lord, chosen as heir while still in his teens, wasn’t as cold as he seemed.
hunks.sol: But no one knew that the Black Dragon Demon Gate’s youngest Young Master, chosen as heir while still in his teens, wasn’t as cold as he seemed.

hunks.baseline: *“……You said your name was Taishan. Come with me.”*
hunks.sol: *“…You said your name was Taishan. Come with me.”*

hunks.baseline: Sama Pyo had found the father of the huge boy who was crying, then carefully buried him. He had been wearing the Black Dragon Demon Gate’s uniform, surrounded by a flock of crows.
hunks.sol: Sama Pyo had found the father of the enormous boy weeping before him. He’d found him in the Black Dragon Demon Gate’s uniform, surrounded by crows, and buried him with care.

hunks.baseline: And Sama Pyo had made his first friend.
hunks.sol: And for the first time in his life, Sama Pyo had made a friend.

hunks.baseline: A friend more precious than family—the only one who cared for him more than his own father did.
hunks.sol: A friend more precious than family—the only person who cared for him more than his own father did.

hunks.baseline: But he hadn’t imagined that he would make other friends more than a decade later.
hunks.sol: But he’d never imagined he would make more friends over a decade later.

hunks.baseline: “Living with them taught me that in the end, everything changes according to the choices I make.”
hunks.sol: “Living with them taught me that, in the end, everything depends on the choices I make.”

hunks.baseline: Despite its grand name, it had fewer than ten members. Among them, Sama Pyo had found a new path he’d never known existed.
hunks.sol: Despite its grand name, it had fewer than ten members. Among them, Sama Pyo had found a path he’d never known existed.

hunks.baseline: They always trusted one another and fought together, and that was how they overcame each crisis.
hunks.sol: They trusted one another, fought together, and saw each other through every crisis.

hunks.baseline: Perhaps that was why.
Why Sama Pyo had looked back on his past again and again.
hunks.sol: Perhaps that was why Sama Pyo had begun looking back on his life again and again.

hunks.baseline: Why, at some point, he had begun to feel something unfamiliar toward his father, a man of ice and stone.
hunks.sol: Why, at some point, he had begun to feel something unfamiliar toward his merciless father.

hunks.baseline: “Then, out of nowhere, I thought: when you look at it closely, you’re a rather pitiable man.”
hunks.sol: “It occurred to me that you might be rather pitiable yourself.”

hunks.baseline: “You probably weren’t like this from the start. Little by little, ambition took hold of you. And one day, you began using any means necessary.”
hunks.sol: “You probably weren’t like this from the start. Ambition took hold of you little by little. Then one day, you stopped caring what it took to get what you wanted.”

hunks.baseline: The son who once couldn’t bear to meet his father’s cold gaze was gone.
hunks.sol: Gone was the son who couldn’t bear to meet his father’s cold gaze.

hunks.baseline: Now, in this moment, Sama Pyo looked at his father, who stood on the brink of death, his eyes calm but full of sorrow.
hunks.sol: Now Sama Pyo looked at his dying father with calm, sorrowful eyes.

hunks.baseline: “It wasn’t an accident.”
hunks.sol: “It wasn’t a coincidence.”

hunks.baseline: “I didn’t happen to come back. I came to see you through your final moments. Not as the heir of the Black Night King, but as the son who carries Sima Gong’s blood.”
hunks.sol: “I didn’t come back by chance. I came to be with you at the end. Not as the Black Night King’s heir, but as Sima Gong’s son.”

hunks.baseline: “Do you know?”
hunks.sol: “Do you know something?”

hunks.baseline: Sama Pyo sat in the pool of blood and met his father’s eyes. Watching his trembling pupils, he continued slowly.
hunks.sol: Sama Pyo sat in the pool of blood and met his father’s eyes. Watching them tremble, he continued slowly.

hunks.baseline: “No son in this world can kill his father.”
hunks.sol: “There is no son in this world who can kill his father.”

hunks.baseline: “I’ll tell them everything myself. I’ll also confess what a pathetic son I’ve been—turning a blind eye to your betrayal even though I knew the truth.”
hunks.sol: “I’ll tell them everything myself. I’ll tell them about the pathetic son who knew of his father’s betrayal and tried not to see it.”

hunks.baseline: “I’m not asking to be forgiven. I’m choosing to bear it.”
hunks.sol: “I’m not asking to be forgiven. I’m going to bear the consequences.”

hunks.baseline: At that peaceful answer, as if he had accepted everything, Sima Gong could say nothing.
hunks.sol: There was such peace in his answer, such acceptance, that Sima Gong could say nothing.

hunks.baseline: He could only struggle to hold back a feeling he’d forgotten for so long, one that had suddenly come back to him here, today.
hunks.sol: He could only struggle to hold back a feeling he’d long forgotten—a feeling he had remembered only here, today.

hunks.baseline: As his vision slowly dimmed, his breath grew short, hinting at the end.
hunks.sol: His vision slowly darkened. His breathing grew short.

hunks.baseline: “You asked why I did it. Why I, who’d spent my whole life chasing survival and practical gain, made such a foolish choice…”
hunks.sol: “You asked me why I did it. Why I, who spent my whole life chasing survival and gain, made such a foolish choice…”

hunks.baseline: “I, your father…”
hunks.sol: “I… This father of yours…”

hunks.baseline: Facing the son who had returned to see his father’s last moments, Sima Gong squeezed out his remaining strength to speak.
hunks.sol: Facing the son who had returned to be with him at the end, Sima Gong used all the strength he had left to force out the words.

hunks.baseline: He didn’t even realize that this was his final breath.
hunks.sol: He didn’t even realize he had drawn his final breath.

hunks.baseline: His head suddenly drooped.
hunks.sol: His head fell to one side.

hunks.baseline: The son looked toward his father, who had met death in a wretched state, as if paying for the sins of his life. Then he whispered quietly.
hunks.sol: To his father, who had died so wretchedly, as if burdened by the deeds of his life, the son whispered, “I heard you. Clearly.”

hunks.baseline: “I heard you. Clearly.”
The pool of blood soaking father and son trembled faintly as Sama Pyo’s shoulders began to shake.
hunks.sol: Sama Pyo’s shoulders began to shake. The pool of blood soaking father and son trembled with them.

hunks.baseline: Highly trained hunting dogs always obeyed their master’s commands.
hunks.sol: Highly trained hunting dogs always obey their master’s commands.

hunks.baseline: They fixed their eyes on the prey their master pointed out, bared their teeth and growled, then, the moment their leash was released, charged forward with all their strength and tore into it.
hunks.sol: They fix their eyes on the prey he points out, bare their teeth and growl. The moment he slips their leashes, they race forward and tear into it with all their strength.

hunks.baseline: Until their prey stopped breathing.
hunks.sol: Until their prey stops breathing.

hunks.baseline: Or until their master ordered them to stop hunting and return.
hunks.sol: Or until their master orders them to stop and return.

hunks.baseline: A fierce, piercing whistle and a flash of light came from the side.
hunks.sol: A piercing whistle came from my side, accompanied by a flash of light.

hunks.baseline: The Sword Energy that surged along the white blade and fell toward my crown moved with the lightning-fast speed of a Peak master. But to me, it didn’t.
hunks.sol: The Sword Energy surged along a white blade and fell toward the top of my head with all the speed expected of a Peak master. To me, though, it wasn’t fast.

hunks.baseline: A fraction of a beat later, the slicing sound rang out. Everything within the path of the silver-white spearhead had been cut apart.
hunks.sol: A fraction of a beat later came the slicing sound. Everything in the silver-white spearhead’s path had been cut apart.

hunks.baseline: The Sword Energy went out like a candle before the wind.
hunks.sol: The Sword Energy, snuffed out like a candle in the wind.

hunks.baseline: The sword that held that mighty energy.
hunks.sol: The blade that had carried that mighty energy.

hunks.baseline: And finally, the body of the person who had launched this futile attack.
hunks.sol: And finally, the body of the man who had made the futile attack.

hunks.baseline: A tremendous fountain of blood burst from the body, split cleanly without a single ragged edge. But I didn’t even blink at the gruesome sight.
hunks.sol: A tremendous fountain of blood burst from his cleanly severed body. I didn’t blink at the sight.

hunks.baseline: Neither did the other hunting dogs charging from every direction, even now.
hunks.sol: Neither did the other hunting dogs charging me from every direction.

hunks.baseline: I drove my spearhead into the chest of the first enemy charging straight at me, then crushed the face of another who came at me from the blind spot with one punch. At the same time, I yanked out the embedded spearhead and swung it.
hunks.sol: I drove my spearhead into the chest of the first one coming straight at me. With my other hand, I crushed the face of an enemy lunging from my blind spot. Then I yanked the embedded spearhead free and swung it.

hunks.baseline: Three Peak masters fell as their dying cries served as their last words.
hunks.sol: Three Peak masters fell with dying cries in place of last words.

hunks.baseline: But the battle frenzy sweeping across the blood-soaked snowfield showed no sign of easing.
hunks.sol: But the frenzy of battle sweeping across the blood-soaked snowfield showed no sign of easing.

hunks.baseline: The Dark Heaven cultists charged in without allowing even the briefest gap, rushing to fill the space left behind.
hunks.sol: The Dark Heaven cultists rushed in to fill the gaps without giving me a moment’s pause.

hunks.baseline: Looking at their blank expressions and emotionless eyes, I felt the crushing exhaustion weighing down my whole body.
hunks.sol: At the sight of their blank faces and eyes devoid of feeling, I felt an exhaustion so deep it weighed down my whole body.

hunks.baseline: I had neither the time nor the reason to count every enemy who had died by my hand.
hunks.sol: I had neither the time nor the reason to count every enemy I’d killed.

hunks.baseline: I just had to fight. Keep knocking them down.
hunks.sol: I could only fight. Keep knocking them down.

hunks.baseline: Those hunting dogs, those moths to the flame, blindly carrying out their final orders even though the master who held their leash was gone.
hunks.sol: Those hunting dogs, those moths blindly carrying out their final order even though the master who held their leashes was gone.

hunks.baseline: It was the only way to end this blood-soaked battle, and the only way to save as many allies as possible.
hunks.sol: It was the only way to end this bloody battle and save as many of our people as I could.

hunks.baseline: So I had no choice but to cling with all my strength to the thread of consciousness that felt ready to snap at any moment.
hunks.sol: So I clung with all my strength to the thread of consciousness that felt ready to snap at any moment.

hunks.baseline: I muttered the words to myself and charged toward the enemy.
hunks.sol: I called to them in my head and charged.

hunks.baseline: That was when my vision began to fade.
hunks.sol: That was when my vision faded.

hunks.baseline: A red alarm bell rang in my head.
hunks.sol: An alarm blared in my head.

hunks.baseline: My mental strength had reached its limit long ago. Now, unable to endure any longer, it was sending me a warning.
hunks.sol: My mind had reached its limit long ago. Now it was sending me a warning it could no longer hold back.

hunks.baseline: But by the time I gritted my teeth and forced my eyes open, it was already too late.
hunks.sol: But by the time I gritted my teeth and forced my eyes wide, it was already too late.

hunks.baseline: From my slanted, blurry view, a dozen blades came raining down on my body as it staggered without my realizing it.
hunks.sol: My view had tilted. A dozen blades were raining down on my body, which had staggered without my even realizing it.

hunks.baseline: Faintly. Slowly.
hunks.sol: They looked faint. Slow.

hunks.baseline: The problem was that, as keen as my eyes were, the brain that needed to send quick commands to move my body had frozen like stone.
hunks.sol: My eyesight was still sharp enough to follow them. The problem was my brain: the part that needed to tell my body to move had frozen like stone.

hunks.baseline: In the slowed-down world, I cursed under my breath.
hunks.sol: I cursed inwardly as the world slowed around me.

hunks.baseline: These men weren’t the Blood-Sword Demon Lord, the Grand Mage, or even close to the Black Ghosts.
hunks.sol: These men were no Blood-Sword Demon Lord or Grand Mage. They couldn’t even compare to the Black Ghosts.

hunks.baseline: No—they were far weaker.
hunks.sol: They fell far short.

hunks.baseline: The gap was so wide that under normal circumstances, I would’ve scoffed at them.
hunks.sol: Under normal circumstances, I would’ve scoffed at the difference between us.

hunks.baseline: Even so, I had a gut feeling I wouldn’t be able to dodge all their attacks.
hunks.sol: Even so, I knew I couldn’t dodge every blade.

hunks.baseline: And, even as my body refused to move, one ridiculous thought crossed my mind.
hunks.sol: And while my body refused to move, one ridiculous thought crossed my mind.

hunks.baseline: *If I level up, does that maybe heal me even if my limbs get cut off?*
hunks.sol: *If I level up, would it heal me even if my limbs got cut off?*

hunks.baseline: Fortunately, nothing happened that forced me to worry about the unpleasant first-time experience only someone like Cheongpung might look forward to.
hunks.sol: Fortunately, I didn’t have to worry about that unpleasant first experience—the sort only someone like Cheongpung might enjoy.

hunks.baseline: The next moment, an enormous whistle rang out from somewhere and swept all my worries away.
hunks.sol: The next moment, an enormous rush of air sounded from somewhere and swept my worries away.

hunks.baseline: Over the shoulders of the enemies charging toward me, a huge shadow suddenly surged upward. Along with it, the two-section staff—big and beautiful, just like its name—sliced through the air like a bolt of lightning.
hunks.sol: A huge shadow rose over the shoulders of the enemies charging toward me. With it came a two-section staff, big and beautiful just as its name suggested, cleaving through the air like lightning.

hunks.baseline: If someone asked whether I’d ever seen five heads blown away with a single whack of a bat, I’d nod without hesitation.
hunks.sol: If anyone ever asked whether I’d seen five heads knocked flying with a single swing of a bat, I could nod without hesitation.

hunks.baseline: I could even tell them the name of the top prospect who’d be bombing today’s modern Major League, now turned into a playground for Awakened Ones.
hunks.sol: I could even name the top prospect who’d tear through the modern Major Leagues, now a playground for Awakened Ones.

hunks.baseline: Of course, that lunatic hulk would introduce himself before anyone else could tell you.
hunks.sol: Of course, that lunatic hulk would introduce himself before anyone else got the chance.

hunks.baseline: Starting with Namho, perched on the shoulder of Taishan—who had just delivered a line to rival even Julius Caesar—familiar faces burst out like streaks of light.
hunks.sol: Starting with Namho, perched on the shoulder of Taishan—who had just delivered a line to make Julius Caesar weep—familiar faces burst onto the scene like streaks of light.

hunks.baseline: “Young Master! No, Benefactor! No, Captain!”
hunks.sol: “Young Master! No, Benefactor! No, Pavilion Master!”

hunks.baseline: Ju Hwaran split an enemy’s skull while blurting out a three-step change of address that even Transformers would’ve had trouble keeping up with.
hunks.sol: Ju Hwaran split an enemy’s skull while changing how she addressed me three times in a breath. Even a Transformer would’ve struggled to keep up.

hunks.baseline: “Fools! How dare you try to harm the Captain! Your courage is admirable, but to do that, you’ll have to get through me—the Captain’s right arm and heart! I, Hyuk Mu—whoa, shit!”
hunks.sol: “Fools! You dare try to harm the Captain? Your courage is admirable, but first you’ll have to get past me—the Captain’s right arm and heart! I, Hyuk Mu—whoa, shit!”

hunks.baseline: Hyuk Mujin had charged in with a grand entrance, only to stumble back in a panic when an unexpectedly stronger enemy counterattacked.
hunks.sol: Hyuk Mujin had charged in with a grand entrance, only to scramble backward when his opponent’s counterattack proved stronger than he’d expected.

hunks.baseline: “Uh, does that guy know how to fight without running his mouth?”
hunks.sol: “Uh, does that guy know how to fight with his mouth shut?”

hunks.baseline: “You should start by keeping yours shut.”
hunks.sol: “You should try shutting yours first.”

hunks.baseline: *Thrust!*
hunks.sol: *Stab, stab!*

hunks.baseline: The four syllables suddenly slipped out of my mouth. The middle-aged man, a former mounted bandit, twisted his already fearsome face.
hunks.sol: The name slipped out before I knew it. The middle-aged man, a former mounted bandit, twisted his already fearsome face.

hunks.baseline: “Not Black Horse—White Horse! I’m Ma Junggeol, eldest of the Seven Masters of Baekma Bang! Who do you think I went through all this shit for? And you forgot me…!”
hunks.sol: “Not Black Horse—White Horse! I’m Ma Junggeol, eldest of the Seven Masters of Baekma Bang! Who do you think went through all this shit for you? And you forgot me…!”

hunks.baseline: At Ju Hwaran’s chilling warning, Ma Junggeol clamped his mouth shut. A laugh escaped me before I knew it.
hunks.sol: Ma Junggeol clamped his mouth shut at Ju Hwaran’s chilling warning. A laugh escaped me.

hunks.baseline: Just because it was nice to see.
hunks.sol: It was just good to see them.

hunks.baseline: Because I knew we hadn’t lost anyone.
hunks.sol: To know we hadn’t lost anyone.

hunks.baseline: Because I could see the one last person I’d thought I’d never meet again.
hunks.sol: To see the last person, the one I’d thought I might never see again.

hunks.baseline: At my abrupt question, Sama Pyo, who I hadn’t even seen arrive, shrugged.
hunks.sol: Sama Pyo, who I hadn’t even seen arrive, shrugged.
